turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: Well, my feathered friend, let me try to break it down for you in a simple way. You see, our planet Earth rotates on its axis as it orbits the sun. This rotation causes day and night. But, it's important to remember that we define "day" as the time the sun is above our horizon and "night" when it's below. So, when we say "morning," it's the start of the sun being above our horizon, and that's the start of our day. Similarly, "evening" is the end of the sun being above our horizon, and that's the start of our night. So, even though the stars might be out during what we call the "morning," they are actually part of the night sky from Earth's perspective. Does that help?
